content: The Spotted jelly, scientifically known as Mastigias papua and commonly referred to as the lagoon jelly, is a species of jellyfish predominantly found in the South Pacific region. Unlike many other jellyfish, this species does not possess a single centralized mouth. Instead, it has multiple smaller mouth openings located on its oral arms, which facilitate feeding. These jellyfish primarily consume zooplankton as their main source of nutrition. In Japan, particularly in areas along the Pacific coast, Spotted jellies are often sold as novelty pets. They are typically accompanied by photoautotrophic phytoplankton, which are included to support their care. Locally, they are referred to as takokurage (タコクラゲ), a term that translates to octopod jelly or rammer jelly. The lifespan of these jellyfish is relatively short, averaging around four months. They are most active during the warmer months, specifically from mid-summer to early fall.
